surprises.description: Q3 gross margin came in at 57.3%, below the preview’s roughly 59% expectation and down 178 basis points sequentially. Management attributed the shortfall to unfavorable DME revenue mix from distributor stocking dynamics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 gross margin was 57.3%” and was “down 178 basis points sequentially and below expectations due to unfavorable DME revenue mix from distributor stocking dynamics.”

surprises.description: The FDA asked Beta Bionics to withdraw the 3D Intelligence 510(k) submission, with resubmission now planned for mid-Q4 and clearance likely in 2027. The preview flagged timing risk, but this is a concrete regulatory setback; management said the questions concerned simulator validation, not the algorithm or outcomes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA requested withdrawal of the 3D Intelligence 510(k) submission over simulator validation questions (not algorithm or outcome concerns), with resubmission planned for mid-Q4 2026 and clearance likely in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for re-inspection status and timing on the 3D Intelligence 510(k) (submitted 9/14/26)” and the bear case included “any ... 3D Intelligence delay.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its FY26 revenue guidance by $3 million, to $124 million, while leaving the high end at $126 million. That is better than the preview’s base case of reiterating the $121–126 million range, though it falls short of a high-end guide increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of full year 2026 revenue guidance to $124 million-$126 million (from $121 million-$126 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “FY26 $121–126M reiterated”; the bull case called for “FY26 raised/narrowed to the high end (≥$126M).”

surprises.description: Management reduced the maximum potential Q4 revenue deferral from patients waiting for Mint from $10 million to $8.5 million, indicating a smaller near-term headwind than the preview’s stated framing. It still expects to more than recover the deferral in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The potential Q4 revenue deferral from patients awaiting Mint was reduced to up to $8.5 million (from up to $10 million), with management expecting to more than make up the deferral in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 9/14 cut was attributed to “up to $10M” of Q4 deferral, recapturable in 2027.

surprises.description: Cash and investments ended Q3 at about $374 million, above the preview’s estimated $330–345 million. The preview expected roughly $140 million of net proceeds from the offering, versus approximately $161 million reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a public offering raising approximately $161 million in net proceeds, ending Q3 with about $374 million in cash, equivalents, and investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 ended with $225.2M; +$140.1M net from the September raise, less ~$20–25M of Q3 burn and Mint capex → ~$330–345M expected.”

surprises.description: Management supplied a favorable per-patient revenue comparison for Mint: roughly six times the monthly revenue from iLet DME supplies. The preview identified Mint economics as a major unknown but did not provide an expected per-patient comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mint generating roughly 6x the monthly revenue per patient versus iLet DME supply revenue of around $70 per month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “quantified 2027 Mint revenue framing” the “single biggest swing factor for the multiple” and said the base case had “no new quantification.”
